territorial_scope.description: Extends to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland, so applies across the United Kingdom.

evidence.quote: This Act extends to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.

summary.short: Bill requiring regulations to create an AI Authority to coordinate regulators, support sandboxes and accredit AI auditors, and to impose AI officer, training-data record, consent, labelling and third-party audit duties on AI businesses across the UK. The Act comes into force on the day it is passed.
summary.long: Requires the Secretary of State, by regulations, to create an AI Authority to coordinate regulators, assess AI risks, support sandboxes and accredit independent AI auditors (s.1). The Authority must have regard to principles including safety, transparency, fairness and proportionality of burdens (s.2). It must work with regulators to construct regulatory sandboxes in which firms test innovative propositions with real consumers (s.3). Regulations must require businesses that develop, deploy or use AI to have a designated AI officer (s.4). Further regulations must require persons training AI to supply the Authority a record of third-party data and intellectual property used and to assure informed consent and copyright compliance; require suppliers of AI products or services to give customers health warnings, labelling and opportunities to consent; and require businesses using AI to allow accredited independent auditors to audit their processes and systems (s.5). The Authority must run a public engagement programme (s.6). Regulations are made by statutory instrument and may create offences and require fees, penalties and fines, with no amounts stated in the Bill (s.8). The Act extends to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland and comes into force on the day it is passed (s.9).

relations.note: Inserts new paragraph (iv) after paragraph (iii) of section 414C(7)(b), covering any development, deployment or use of AI by the company and the name and activities of the AI officer designated under this Act.

notes: Text as introduced (HL Bill 76, ordered to be printed 4 March 2025); no in-force date is stated for regulations under sections 1 to 5, which are left to later regulations. Section 1(2)(i) cites section 5(1)(a)(iv), which does not appear in the text as printed (section 5(1)(a) has only (i) and (ii)). Section 4(1)(a) uses 'designated AI officer' while the section heading says 'AI responsible officers'. Section 7(1)(b) has a stray closing quotation mark. Section 4(2) and section 9(3) refer to the Act itself as the 'Artificial Intelligence (Regulation) Act 2025'; this self-reference is not coded as a relation.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changing legal treatment in the bill. Sections 1 to 9 apply to 'any business which develops, deploys or uses AI' (s.4(1), s.5(1)(c)) without a size test, and s.3(2)(d) 'small scale' is not numeric. Section 8 sets approval procedure, not thresholds. No threshold delegated to regulations was found.
